study type: Nested case-control study within a cohort
cohort: The study participants were 107 pregnant women with spontaneous preterm birth and 432 women delivering at term, selected from a larger cohort of 2000 pregnant women.
finding: Seven bacterial taxa in the cervicovaginal microbiota were significantly associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth, an effect modulated by vaginal b-defensin-2 levels and ethnicity.
